mcq.QUESTION_DESC: Which data structure follows the Last In, First Out (LIFO) principle?
Which of the following conditions indicate that a stack is full when implemented using an array of size N?
Suppose an array-based stack has a capacity of 100 elements. If 50 elements are pushed and 20 elements are popped, what is the current position of top?

What will be the output of the following stack operations if implemented using an array of size 5?

push(1) 

push(2) 

push(3) 

pop() 

push(4) 

push(5) 

push(6)
If a stack is implemented using an array, what is the worst-case time complexity of checking if the stack is empty?

sq.ANSWER:
A stack is a linear data structure that follows the Last In, First Out (LIFO) principle, meaning the last element added is the first to be removed. It supports two primary operations:

  • Push: Adds an element to the top of the stack.
  • Pop: Removes the top element from the stack.

Example: Function Calls in a Program

Function calls in programming languages use a stack to manage execution. When a function is called, it is pushed onto the stack, and when it completes execution, it is popped off.

Example Code (C-like pseudocode):

void functionA() { 

    functionB();  // Calls functionB

} 

 

void functionB() { 

    functionC();  // Calls functionC

} 

 

void functionC() { 

    // Function C executes and returns 

} 

 

int main() { 

    functionA();  // Calls functionA

    return 0; 

}

Stack Representation for Function Calls:

  1. main() calls functionA() → Stack: [functionA]
  2. functionA() calls functionB() → Stack: [functionA, functionB]
  3. functionB() calls functionC() → Stack: [functionA, functionB, functionC]
  4. functionC() completes and is popped → Stack: [functionA, functionB]
  5. functionB() completes and is popped → Stack: [functionA]
  6. functionA() completes and is popped → Stack: []

Thus, function calls follow a stack-based approach where the most recently called function completes first.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Describe the concept of a stack with a real-time example using function calls.

sq.ANSWER:
Algorithm: Push Operation in Array-Based Stack

Input: Stack array stack[], maximum size MAX, element item to be pushed
Output: Element is added to the stack

  1. Check if the stack is full:
    • If top == MAX - 1, print "Stack Overflow" and exit.
  2. Increment the top pointer:
    • top = top + 1
  3. Insert the new element:
    • stack[top] = item
  4. End

Pseudocode:

void push(int st[], int val)

{

    if(top == MAX-1)

    {

        printf("\n STACK OVERFLOW");

    }

    else

    {

        top++;

        st[top] = val;

    }

}

 

Example Execution:

 push(10):

  • top = 0
  • Stack → [10]

push(20):

  • top = 1
  • Stack → [10, 20]

 push(30):

  • top = 2
  • Stack → [10, 20, 30]

 push(40):

  • top = 3
  • Stack → [10, 20, 30, 40]

 push(50):

  • top = 4
  • Stack → [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]

 push(60): (Exceeds MAX size)

  • Condition if(top == MAX-1) is true
  • Output: "STACK OVERFLOW"
  • Stack remains → [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]

Thus, the stack follows Last In, First Out (LIFO), and elements are pushed until it reaches the maximum capacity.
sq.QUESTION_DESC: Write an algorithm to implement the Push operation in a stack using an array, and illustrate it with an example.

lq.ANSWER:
The main function controls the user interactions and calls respective stack operations (book, cancel, check latest, and view reservations).

Main Function Algorithm:

  1. Start.
  2. Initialize:
    • Set top = -1 (indicating an empty stack).
    • Define MAX = 3 (maximum ticket reservations allowed).
  3. Repeat Until the User Chooses Exit:
    1. Display the menu options:
      • 1. Book Ticket
      • 2. Cancel Ticket
      • 3. Check Latest Reservation
      • 4. View All Reservations
      • 5. Exit
    2. Ask the user to enter an option.
    3. Perform the corresponding operation:
      • If option = 1:
        • Ask for ticketID (user input).
        • Call bookTicket(tickets, ticketID).
      • If option = 2:
        • Call cancelTicket(tickets).
        • If it returns a valid ticket ID, print "Ticket ID X has been canceled."
      • If option = 3:
        • Call latestReservation(tickets).
        • If it returns a valid ticket ID, print "The latest reserved ticket ID is: X."
      • If option = 4:
        • Call viewReservations(tickets).
      • If option = 5:
        • Exit the program.
    4. Loop back to Step 3 until the user selects Exit.
  4. End.

 

Program:

#include <stdio.h>

#include <stdlib.h>

 

#define MAX 3  // Maximum number of ticket reservations

int tickets[MAX], top = -1;

 

void bookTicket(int tickets[], int ticketID);

int cancelTicket(int tickets[]);

int latestReservation(int tickets[]);

void viewReservations(int tickets[]);

 

int main() {

    int ticketID, option;

   

    do {

        printf("\n***** TICKET BOOKING SYSTEM *****");

        printf("\n1. Book Ticket");

        printf("\n2. Cancel Ticket");

        printf("\n3. Check Latest Reservation");

        printf("\n4. View All Reservations");

        printf("\n5. Exit");

        printf("\nEnter your option: ");

        scanf("%d", &option);

       

        switch(option) {

            case 1:

                printf("\nEnter Ticket ID to book: ");

                scanf("%d", &ticketID);

                bookTicket(tickets, ticketID);

                break;

            case 2:

                ticketID = cancelTicket(tickets);

                if(ticketID != -1)

                    printf("\nTicket ID %d has been canceled.", ticketID);

                break;

            case 3:

                ticketID = latestReservation(tickets);

                if(ticketID != -1)

                    printf("\nThe latest reserved ticket ID is: %d", ticketID);

                break;

            case 4:

                viewReservations(tickets);

                break;

        }

    } while(option != 5);

   

    return 0;

}

 

// Function to book a ticket (Push Operation)

void bookTicket(int tickets[], int ticketID) {

    if(top == MAX - 1) {

        printf("\nBooking failed! The hall is full (STACK OVERFLOW).");

    } else {

        top++;

        tickets[top] = ticketID;

        printf("\nTicket ID %d successfully booked!", ticketID);

    }

}

 

// Function to cancel the latest booked ticket (Pop Operation)

int cancelTicket(int tickets[]) {

    if(top == -1) {

        printf("\nNo reservations to cancel (STACK UNDERFLOW).");

        return -1;

    } else {

        int ticketID = tickets[top];

        top--;

        return ticketID;

    }

}

 

// Function to check the latest reservation (Peek Operation)

int latestReservation(int tickets[]) {

    if(top == -1) {

        printf("\nNo reservations found (STACK EMPTY).");

        return -1;

    } else {

        return tickets[top];

    }

}

 

// Function to display all reservations (Display Stack)

void viewReservations(int tickets[]) {

    if(top == -1) {

        printf("\nNo reservations found (STACK EMPTY).");

    } else {

        printf("\nCurrent Reservations (Top to Bottom):");

        for(int i = top; i >= 0; i--)

            printf("\nTicket ID: %d", tickets[i]);

        printf("\n");

    }

}

lq.QUESTION_DESC:
A ticket booking system for a small cinema hall is designed using an array-based stack to handle customer reservations. The system can hold a maximum of 3 reservations at a time (as defined by MAX = 3). When a customer books a ticket, the reservation is pushed onto the stack. If the hall reaches full capacity, further bookings result in a Stack Overflow error. When a customer cancels a ticket, the last booked ticket is popped from the stack (Last In, First Out).

A customer service agent performs the following operations in order:

  1. Book Ticket (push 101)
  2. Book Ticket (push 102)
  3. Book Ticket (push 103)
  4. Book Ticket (push 104) → System response?
  5. Cancel Ticket (pop) → Which ticket is removed?
  6. Check Current Reservation (peek) → Which ticket remains at the top?
  7. View All Reservations (display) → What is the current stack state?
